correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the derivation block law and its square-zero implications λ=0, A²=0, fA=0. Proved ker(A)=(im A)^perp and a bijection between rank-r square-zero symplectic A and an isotropic r-plane with an invertible symmetric form on its dual. Counted q^(2m-r) compatible f, of which q^r preserve rank r and the others add one. Derived isotropic-frame product and characteristic-two congruence orbits (including stabilizer q^(2k-1)Sp_(2k-2)), yielding the same closed symmetric-matrix count for all characteristics. Confirmed nonzero support only 0..m, and leading q-degrees give rank-m concentration. Exhaustive matrix checks over q=2,3,4,5 for m=1 and q=2,3 for m=2, plus symmetric matrix checks, passed. These finite checks are supplementary rather than infinite certificates.

originality.rationale: A statement-level search and source reading identified general Heisenberg derivation structures, symplectic nilpotent totals, and characteristic-two symmetric-form classification, but not the complete rank polynomial for D²=0 on the full (2m+1)-dimensional Heisenberg algebra with its coupling to central functionals. Neither the known total nilpotent symplectic count nor the prior unconstrained Heisenberg endomorphism rank formula implies the claimed distribution without additional rank-sensitive analysis and a different morphism condition. Residual possibility of equivalent older orbit enumeration is disclosed; database non-detection is not treated as proof of novelty.

value.rationale: A complete exact rank distribution for a natural square-zero subvariety of Der(H_m) across all finite fields and arbitrary dimensions is a substantive enumerative invariant; it is not merely a family of small cases. The sharp forbidden-rank interval m+1..2m+1 and the concentration at maximal allowable rank as q grows distinguish the square-zero derivation condition from generic derivations and Lie homomorphisms. The characteristic-two stabilizer split, although canceling in the final total product, is structurally necessary to understand why the same uniform formula holds in all characteristics. This has plausible use in enumeration of nilpotent derivations, symplectic Lie algebra geometry and degenerations of finite two-step Lie algebras.
